Synagogue Parma

Synagogue · Parma, Italy

The existing synagogue was built in 1866 within the community’s building, purchased in 1822 and left bare of any exterior identifying features. The hall, on the uppermost floor, has an oblong shape, interspersed with pilasters clad in marbled stucco. It features the typical layout of the period, inspired by Catholic churches: opposite the entrance sits the 18 th century aron, originally from the synagogue of Colorno; in front of it is the tevah, made at the same time as the synagogue was designed, as were all the other furnishings. Above the entrance, the hall is enclosed by the women’s gallery.
